ui_info_states:
Spoof: report the typed value.
Skip: leave the real ROM value.
Empty: report an empty value.
Null: remove the field entirely.
Global: apply the value to every app, not only the ones in scope.
ui_info_scope: Which app processes get the spoof - Global (every app), a Whitelist or Blacklist you choose, or Google Play (only the Play Integrity processes).
ui_info_scope_apps: The list of apps that the Whitelist or Blacklist mode applies to.
ui_info_motor_jni: Writes the spoofed values into the android.os.Build fields that apps read from Java.
ui_info_motor_prop_hook: Spoofs the native system properties (ro.build.*) that apps read without going through Java. Per-process (mmap) applies them only inside the targeted apps; Off disables it.
ui_info_prop_method: How the property hook is applied. Per-process (mmap) changes the properties only inside the targeted apps, leaving the rest of the system untouched.
ui_info_motor_drm: Spoofs the Widevine DRM security level that media and streaming apps check: L1 (hardware-backed) or L3 (software). Off disables it.
ui_info_drm_level: The DRM level reported to apps: L1 (hardware-backed) or L3 (software).
ui_info_resetprop: Master switch for rewriting system properties for the whole device at boot.
ui_info_grp_identity: Device identity properties: brand, model, device, fingerprint and so on.
ui_info_grp_version: Android version properties. Changing these can cause boot loops, so they are off by default.
ui_info_grp_boot_state: Verified-boot and bootloader-state properties (for example verifiedbootstate and the lock state).
ui_info_grp_selinux_bootmode: SELinux and boot-mode properties (for example enforcing and normal boot).
ui_info_grp_anti_emulator: Properties that hide emulator or QEMU traces.
ui_info_manufacturer: Also spoof ro.product.manufacturer. Off by default because on some devices it can read as inconsistent.
ui_info_autoupdate: On boot, refresh the profile to the newest matching factory image.
ui_info_version_spoof: Whether to spoof the Android version. Never is the safe choice - spoofing the version can cause boot loops.
